personalitySettings.title: Assistant tone & response style
personalitySettings.maxOutputTokensNote: Caps how long a single response can be — lower is faster and more battery-friendly on phone hardware.
personalitySettings.deepResearchNote: Breaks your question into sub-questions, researches each separately, then synthesizes one answer. Several sequential model calls on the same model — noticeably slower than a normal reply, not multiple AI models running at once. Independent from the response style above: it changes how much research goes into an answer, not its tone — the two combine (e.g. Deep Research + Succinct still synthesizes a short final answer).
personalitySettings.adaptiveRoutingNote: Classifies each message and picks which downloaded model answers it (e.g. a lightweight model for small talk, a stronger one for research/comparison questions), switching between them as needed. On by default and independent from Deep Research — if it fails for any reason, chat falls back to your normal active model automatically, it never leaves you without a response.

personalDocumentsManager.hint: Import your own .txt, .md, .csv, .json, or .pdf notes — indexed on this device only, never uploaded anywhere. PDFs need selectable text (scanned/image-only pages won't extract — there's no OCR), and password-protected PDFs aren't supported.

aboutScreen.title: About BOAR
aboutScreen.airGappedBody: BOAR is an offline-first mobile AI system exploring adaptive model routing, local retrieval, and resource-aware inference. It performs local LLM inference via llama.rn / llama.cpp and local hybrid retrieval (SQLite FTS5 + on-device embeddings) with zero cloud dependencies.
aboutScreen.hardwareBody: Complies with strict mobile field constraints: resident memory remains capped under 12GB RAM using memory-mapped weights (mmap), and total storage is audited against a 50GB storage envelope.
aboutScreen.benchmarkBody: BOAR measures every answer on your own phone: model load time, time to first token, tokens/sec, peak memory and which sources were used. Run the built-in evaluation from Execution Telemetry → 🧪 Evaluate to compare any installed model on the same questions, or drive it from a computer with npm run eval:device.
aboutScreen.repoBody: Source code, quantized model manifests, and offline indexing scripts are available at:

why.shared-pending: This phone's secure hardware couldn't prove the results come from a real phone, which happens on some genuine phones. The run is saved and the BOAR team will review it before it appears on the website.

why.cooldown: Shares from one phone need an hour between them. Try again later.
why.cooldownAt: Shares from one phone need an hour between them. You can share again at {{time}}.
why.network-limited: Many runs were shared from this network today, maybe other phones on the same Wi-Fi. Try again later, or from another connection.
why.rejected: The server refused this run. Only the official BOAR app, up to date, on a real phone can share. The details below say why.
why.offline: No answer from the server. Check the internet connection and try again. Your results are still on the phone.
why.busy: Too many shares right now. Try again in a few minutes.
why.server-error: Something went wrong on the server. Try again in a few minutes; if it keeps happening, export the results and send them to the team.
why.key-failed: This phone couldn't create or use a security key to sign the results, so they can't be shared. Export them instead and send the file to the team.
why.failed: Something unexpected went wrong. Try again, or export the results.
